subject.title: Subagent Health v1 — health classification + sweep-driven recovery

question: Should this v1 expose the nine-state health and next-action contract while enabling automatic sweeper recovery, or should the race fixes land separately before designing that public API?
rationale: The patch combines concrete race fixes with a new public protocol taxonomy and recovery policy; code review can identify defects, but it cannot decide the permanent user-facing lifecycle contract.

options.title: Split race fixes first
options.body: Land the timeout and concurrent orphan-recovery fixes independently, then review the health API and sweep policy as a smaller product change.

options.title: Keep the combined v1
options.body: Retain the combined feature after correcting authoritative-state classification and adding comprehensive live behavior and compatibility proof.

options.title: Defer public health fields
options.body: Keep health observation internal to the sweeper until maintainers settle which statuses and actions should become stable gateway API.

recommendation.title: Split race fixes first
recommendation.body: Land the timeout and concurrent orphan-recovery fixes independently, then review the health API and sweep policy as a smaller product change.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns both the task protocol surface and the current subagent stale-run invariant affected by this decision.
